title: Leavitt's law: a yardstick for cosmic distances
summary: Working as a low-paid plate reader at Harvard College Observatory, Leavitt found that Cepheid stars' brightness is tied to their pulsing period.
why: Gave astronomers their first way to measure distances to other galaxies.

notes.problem: 'Women could not operate the telescopes' carries a 'dubious' tag in the source; replaced with sourced pay and Nobel facts.

unsung.contribution: Discovered the period-luminosity relation of Cepheid variable stars, the key to measuring distances beyond our galaxy.
unsung.recognition: Paid about 30 cents an hour as a plate reader; a 1924 Nobel nomination attempt came three years after she had died.
